item.title: MGM begins journey
item.description: MAHATMA Gandhi Memorial Primary School is making its mark at the inaugural Fiji Primary Schools Badminton Tournament, giving its young players their first opportunity to experience competitive badminton at this level. The three-day tournament began yesterday and continues until tomorrow at the FMF Gymnasium, with MGM fielding eight boys and six girls.
item.content:encoded:
MAHATMA Gandhi Memorial Primary School is making its mark at the inaugural Fiji Primary Schools Badminton Tournament, giving its young players their first opportunity to experience competitive badminton at this level.

The three-day tournament began yesterday and continues until tomorrow at the FMF Gymnasium, with MGM fielding eight boys and six girls.

Team manager Emi Naiteitei said the main focus is to expose the children to competition while helping them develop their skills and confidence.

“First of all, it’s the competition itself. I wanted the children to have a feel of what badminton is, and at the moment they are doing very well,” Naiteitei said.

The historic nature of the tournament has brought excitement to the MGM players, although Naiteitei said some were nervous when they first arrived at the gymnasium.

She encouraged them to stay positive, work hard and keep pushing through their matches.

MGM has set its sights on reaching the quarterfinals, with hopes of progressing further into the semifinals.

However, Naiteitei believes the tournament is about more than results, with the school looking to build a foundation for the players’ future in badminton.

MGM did not participate in the high school badminton tournament earlier this year, but Naiteitei said the school plans to continue training its players after this tournament.

“We will continue with our training to prepare them for the next game, come next year,” she said.

For Naiteitei, that continued training is important in developing the players at grassroots level and potentially preparing them for badminton when they reach secondary school.

She also acknowledged the support of parents, fellow team manager Krishnil Kumar and head of school Mrs Lal in helping the team prepare for the historic competition.

For MGM, the tournament represents an important first step in introducing its young players to competitive badminton and building their confidence for the future.

item.title: A father’s memory, a daughter’s triumph
item.description: THE number 77 on Isabella Ratu’s back tells a story that goes far beyond basketball. It belongs to her late father, the man she remembers as her biggest supporter, the one who took her to training and stood behind her journey in the sport.
item.content:encoded:
THE number 77 on Isabella Ratu’s back tells a story that goes far beyond basketball.

It belongs to her late father, the man she remembers as her biggest supporter, the one who took her to training and stood behind her journey in the sport.

From Tavua, with maternal roots in Cakaudrove, Ratu has carried that support with her as she developed into a leader on the basketball court.

Last weekend, she had another reason to wear the number with pride.

As captain, Ratu led St Joseph’s Secondary School to the Under-19 title at the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball National Championships, defeating defending champions Adi Cakobau School 19–13 in the final.

For Ratu, the championship was the result of faith, preparation and the support of those closest to her.

“Honestly, I just want to thank the Lord because we wouldn’t make it this far without him,” she said.

Ratu arrived at the tournament confident because of the work she had put in long before the championship began, training in the mornings, afternoons and nights.

“It was all about preparation before,” she said.

Her role as captain brought another challenge.

With more than 12 players in the squad but only 12 allowed on the bench, difficult decisions had to be made during the tournament. At one point, one player had to sit out.

“It’s not an easy decision to make, but we made that as our fuel to go through to the finals so that she could play with us,” Ratu said.

That decision reflects the togetherness she associates with St Joseph’s.

For Ratu, representing the school is about more than competing. It is about the values, sisterhood and bond she has built with her teammates and the younger players.

“The name carries more than itself,” she said.

Now, with a national school title secured, Ratu is looking beyond the school court.

Her ambition over the next five years is to continue her studies while working towards representing Fiji at the Pacific Games.

She has not yet had discussions about selection opportunities, but she believes the championship gave her a platform to demonstrate what she can offer.

Whatever comes next, Ratu will carry the lessons from this campaign with her, and, most importantly, the number 77.

Her victory was dedicated to her mother and two brothers, while her father remained at the heart of her motivation.

And if she could speak to the little girl who first picked up a basketball, Ratu knows exactly what she would say.

“Keep going. It does get better. You do get better and never give up that passion and that love you have for your sport.”

For Ratu, the achievement is one she can only describe in two simple words: “God did.”

item.title: Veterans return | Veterans tournament to promote healthy living
item.description: FORMER footballers will have the opportunity to return to the field and showcase their skills when the RC Manubhai/Apco Coatings International Veteran’s Tournament is held in Ba from September 11 to 13. The three-day tournament will be played at 4R Stadium at Govind Park and the Fiji Football Association Academy grounds in Ba, alongside the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament.
item.content:encoded:
FORMER footballers will have the opportunity to return to the field and showcase their skills when the RC Manubhai/Apco Coatings International Veteran’s Tournament is held in Ba from September 11 to 13.

The three-day tournament will be played at 4R Stadium at Govind Park and the Fiji Football Association Academy grounds in Ba, alongside the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament.

The tournament, organised for veteran players, will feature two divisions the Over-40 and the newly introduced Over-50 competition.

The Over-40 division will be limited to the first 16 teams, while the Over-50 division will accommodate up to eight teams.

Teams wishing to participate will pay an entry fee of $500, with registration forms available from the Fiji FA Competitions Department. Entries close on August 30.

Prize money will be awarded to the champions and runners-up in both divisions, adding further incentive for former players to get back on the field and compete.

However, organisers say the tournament is about more than competition and prizes.

The event is being promoted as an opportunity for former players to remain active, maintain a healthy lifestyle and help combat non-communicable diseases (NCDs).

The tournament will also support the welfare of former footballers, with proceeds from the event assisting with the education of their children.

item.title: Young shuttlers chase glory
item.description: A RECORD 261 young badminton players from 22 primary schools are making history this week as Badminton Fiji hosts the country’s first-ever National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva. The three-day tournament, which began yesterday and ends tomorrow, has attracted players from Suva, Nadi, Lautoka, Navunikabi in the Namosi Highlands and Nabouwalu in Bua.
item.content:encoded:
A RECORD 261 young badminton players from 22 primary schools are making history this week as Badminton Fiji hosts the country’s first-ever National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva.

The three-day tournament, which began yesterday and ends tomorrow, has attracted players from Suva, Nadi, Lautoka, Navunikabi in the Namosi Highlands and Nabouwalu in Bua.

Girls make up 49 per cent of the field, highlighting the sport’s growing participation and focus on gender inclusion.

The tournament is the first national competitive pathway for primary school players aged 11 to 13 and under, building on the Fiji Secondary Schools Tournament, which has been running for 29 years.

It is also the largest badminton tournament staged in Fiji, with participation rising from 105 players at the 2025 Secondary Schools Tournament to 168 in May this year before reaching 261 at this week’s primary schools event.

Competition is divided into Teams and Individuals sections, with schools competing in a five-match format of doubles, singles, doubles, singles and doubles to determine the best school teams.

The under-13 and U11 players will also compete in elimination and consolation draws for individual honours.

The tournament forms part of Badminton Fiji’s wider player-development pathway.

Through a partnership with the Zespri AIMS Games in Tauranga, New Zealand, two standout primary school players will travel to compete at the 2026 AIMS Games shortly after the tournament.

Badminton Fiji will also select its first-ever Fiji U15 national squad following the competition.

The squad will comprise 25 girls and 25 boys selected from leading performers in the Secondary Schools U15 and Primary Schools U13 and U11 divisions.

The selected players will undergo a one-year elite training programme as Badminton Fiji works to develop a sustainable pathway into its U17 and U19 national squads.

The long-term objective is to build a core group of players capable of contributing to Fiji’s high-performance programme and targeting podium success at the 2031 Pacific Games in Tonga.

The tournament is supported by a Badminton World Federation grant and sponsorship from SportsWorld, CKs Mega Bargain, Damodar Cinemas, GEM Fiji Ltd and Punjas Fiji.

item.title: Elite pathway remains key for local hopefuls
item.description: LOCAL rugby league players will have to raise their level and gain greater exposure to elite competition before they can come into consideration for the Vodafone Fiji Bati. That is the message from Bati head coach Mick Potter, who says he has been keeping an eye on domestic competitions but is not currently considering locally based players for selection.
item.content:encoded:
LOCAL rugby league players will have to raise their level and gain greater exposure to elite competition before they can come into consideration for the Vodafone Fiji Bati.

That is the message from Bati head coach Mick Potter, who says he has been keeping an eye on domestic competitions but is not currently considering locally based players for selection.

Potter says the standard required to play international rugby league means players need to be exposed to an elite environment where they can develop the skills, fitness and preparation needed to compete at the highest level.

While local players are not presently in his plans, Potter says that does not close the door on their international ambitions.

He says he has considerable respect for players competing in Fiji and believes they can eventually reach the standard required to wear the Bati jersey.

The challenge, however, is for those players to bridge the gap between domestic competition and the demands of international rugby league.

With 45 days remaining before the Rugby League World Cup, Potter is also working against the clock to finalise his squad.

The coach says the Bati have not settled on their final playing group, although the selectors have a clear indication of the players they want for the tournament.

Fiji faces a demanding World Cup campaign after being drawn alongside defending champions Australia, New Zealand and the Cook Islands.

item.title: Lomani confident Fijiana XV can rise to challenge
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani says the side has returned to camp with renewed determination as they prepare for a tough Test against Japan on September 4 and the upcoming WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong from September 13-26. The Fijiana XV resumed training this week following a short break after their two-Test series against the South African women’s team.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV captain Kolora Lomani says the side has returned to camp with renewed determination as they prepare for a tough Test against Japan on September 4 and the upcoming WXV Global Series Challenger in Hong Kong from September 13-26.

The Fijiana XV resumed training this week following a short break after their two-Test series against the South African women’s team.

Lomani said it had been a demanding week in camp, with the players focusing on areas where they fell short during the South Africa matches.

“It’s been going well after the two games against the South African women’s team,” Lomani said.

Lomani said one of the key messages to the players was the importance of understanding their individual responsibilities and delivering their roles for the team.

The squad has reviewed footage from the South Africa Tests, with players encouraged to study their performances individually and work collectively as units.

“We had to go back and look at our clips and do our homework as individuals and as a unit,” she said.

“We’ve been doing that during the week and hopefully we can make those changes leading into next week’s game and the WXV.”

Lomani believes the Fijiana XV have plenty of potential, highlighting the work being done by the forwards in the set pieces as one of the team’s major strengths.

“The forwards have been working hard with their set pieces, especially the lineouts and scrums,” she said.

“Our strength is through the forwards, and obviously we’ve got our backline as well.

“We just have to get the forwards doing their job and running up the middle, then spread the ball out wide where we can.”

Lomani expects a fierce contest against Japan, a team Fiji has only faced once before.

“They’re a really strong team and they play their rugby with heart,” she said.

“We’re looking forward to a good game against Japan.”

Lomani also thanked the Fijiana XV supporters for their continued encouragement as the team prepares to represent Fiji overseas.

item.title: New faces in squad please Politini
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi Senior Men’s head coach Cohan Politini was pleased with his side’s improved second-half performance after maintaining their unbeaten run in Round Five of the Skipper Cup Competition against Taveuni at Churchill Park in Lautoka last week. Politini said his players had prepared thoroughly for the encounter, knowing Taveuni would provide a tough challenge following their impressiv
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi Senior Men’s head coach Cohan Politini was pleased with his side’s improved second-half performance after maintaining their unbeaten run in Round Five of the Skipper Cup Competition against Taveuni at Churchill Park in Lautoka last week.

Politini said his players had prepared thoroughly for the encounter, knowing Taveuni would provide a tough challenge following their impressive 32-22 victory over Nadroga at Lawaqa Park in Round Four.

“We were prepared for that. We knew that Taveuni would give us a good game after they won against Nadroga,” Politini said.

“We prepared very well during the week, and it was more of a relief that we put on a better second half than we’ve done in the past four games.”

Nadi also used the match as an opportunity to introduce fresh talent, with four players making their debut and three others joining the squad from the development team.

Politini said the seven new faces provided an opportunity to rest some of the more experienced players while strengthening the team’s depth.

The Jetsetters faced a difficult opening half and trailed at the break, but Politini said his message to the players was simple.

“The message was just to stick to our systems. We know how our systems work,” he said.

“I was glad that we were down because it actually brought out the best in the boys in the second half, and they answered the call.”

Despite remaining unbeaten in the competition, Politini said keeping the players grounded remained a key focus for the coaching staff.

He said maintaining the right culture, discipline and consistency in training was crucial, as performances on the field were often influenced by what happened away from rugby.

Nadi will now turn their attention to Navosa in Round Six.

Politini expects another difficult contest when the Jetsetters host the improving Navosa side at King Charles Park in Nadi this Saturday.

“It’s a final every week. Navosa is a very good team and they’re climbing up, so we’re going to prepare extra well for them.”

item.title: Navua targets long awaited BOG triumph
item.description: Former Navua football head coach Saiyad Ali believes the district side has the consistency, experience and strengthened squad needed to mount another serious challenge for the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants (BOG) title. The prestigious tournament will be held from September 4-6 and September 12-13, with Navua again among the teams expected to feature strongly at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.
item.content:encoded:
Former Navua football head coach Saiyad Ali believes the district side has the consistency, experience and strengthened squad needed to mount another serious challenge for the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants (BOG) title.

The prestigious tournament will be held from September 4-6 and September 12-13, with Navua again among the teams expected to feature strongly at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

Ali said Navua had established itself as one of the country’s most consistent football teams over the past five years, regularly reaching the business end of major competitions despite falling short of winning a title.

“We have been playing one or two finals every season for the last five years and the team has been knocking on the door so many times,” Ali said.

“They have already played six or seven finals, and they haven’t won one yet.”

However, Ali believes this year’s BOG could provide another important opportunity for the side to finally break through.

He said Navua had retained and strengthened its core group of players, which could give the team an advantage over its rivals.

“This season, especially in the BOG, I have seen that they have strengthened the same team.”

“I think that gives them the edge over the other teams, and I think the preparation has been going well. The team is in camp now and they are all looking forward to a very good tournament.”

Ali also expects a highly competitive tournament, saying the standard of football in Fiji has risen following the introduction of the OFC Pro League.

He said the return of players from the professional competition, including national representatives and overseas players from countries such as Vanuatu, had added further quality and excitement to the local game.

“The competition level has gone up,” Ali said. Navua takes on Suva in the opening match of the tournament at 1pm on Friday.
